focus_areas.area: EC2 instance vulnerabilities (CVEs, patches, agent status)
Patch compliance and missing security patches
Severity severity distribution and risk scoring

rule.title: Critical CVE Detection
rule.description: CVEs with CVSS >= 9.0 are Critical findings
rule.action: Flag all Critical/High severity CVEs from Inspector v2

rule.title: Unpatched Instances
rule.description: EC2 instances without patches for 30+ days are High risk
rule.metric: Check PatchableStatus in SSM Compliance data

rule.title: Inspector Agent Status
rule.description: EC2 instances without Inspector agent are Medium risk
rule.action: Flag instances with AgentStatus != ACTIVE or HEALTHY

rule.title: Container Image Vulnerabilities
rule.description: Container images in ECR with unscanned or High/Critical CVEs

rule.title: Lambda Dependency Vulnerabilities
rule.description: Lambda functions with vulnerable dependencies (via CodeGuruReviewer)
rule.action: Analyze Lambda layer dependencies for known CVEs

rule.title: Missing Security Patches
rule.description: Packages with available security patches not installed
rule.metric: Count MissingPatches in SSM patch compliance reports

focus.check: Findings sorted by severity (Critical, High, Medium, Low)
Package vulnerability details (name, version, fix available)
Last patch date (>30 days old is concerning)
Images with ImageScanStatus == FAILED or unscanned
Instances with AgentStatus != ACTIVE or HEALTHY

irrefutable_evidence_guide.requirement: Every VULNS finding MUST include in evidence_snippet the exact AWS metadata that proves the claim:
irrefutable_evidence_guide.general_rule: Do not make generic assertions. Include the exact field values from AWS API responses (JSON snippets) that justify the finding.

template.title: Apply Security Patch for Critical CVE

steps.step: 1. Identify affected EC2 instances from vulnerability report
2. Create snapshot or AMI backup before patching
3. Use AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager to apply patches
4. Schedule maintenance window for automatic patching
5. Verify patch installation with SSM compliance check
6. Re-run Inspector scan to confirm vulnerability resolved

template.title: Enable Inspector Agent on EC2 Instance

steps.step: 1. Go to EC2 > Instances > [Instance]
2. Check IAM role has AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore and SSMPatchAssociation
3. Use Systems Manager to run command: aws ssm send-command for agent installation
4. Or: Launch new instance with AmazonInspector2AgentPolicy IAM role
5. Verify agent status in Inspector console (should show ACTIVE)
6. Allow 5-10 minutes for first scan to complete
1. Identify vulnerable image from ECR scan results
2. Update base image in Dockerfile to latest patched version
3. Update application dependencies to fixed versions
4. Rebuild and re-tag image in ECR
5. Run ECR image scan on new image
6. Verify scan shows no High/Critical vulnerabilities
7. Deploy updated image to production
1. Review CodeGuruReviewer findings for Lambda function
2. Identify vulnerable packages in requirements.txt or package.json
3. Update packages to patched versions
4. Test Lambda function locally with updated dependencies
5. Create new Lambda layer with updated dependencies
6. Deploy updated Lambda version
7. Re-run CodeGuruReviewer scan to confirm resolution

severity_calibration.note: Vulns severity is CVSS-based from Inspector v2
severity_calibration.critical: CVSS >= 9.0 OR Critical CVE in active workload
severity_calibration.high: CVSS 7.0-8.9 OR High CVE affecting multiple instances
severity_calibration.medium: CVSS 4.0-6.9 OR patch available but not urgently needed
